reference.notes:
I've implemented the spec in `src/_path.ts`. Every test passes: both new suites and the existing suite, 430 tests in total.

There are two changes:
- **The pattern:** `_EXTNAME_RE` is now `/.(\.[^./]+|\.)$/`. A dot at the very end now counts as the extension `"."`, provided some character comes before it. So `"index."`, `"foo.."`, `"..."`, `"/.."` and `"C:\.."` all give `"."`. An empty path still gives `""`, and so does a path ending in `/` or `\`, because the dot has to be the last character.
- **`extname`:** it now returns `""` straight away when the input is exactly `"."` or `".."`. This check runs on the raw input before backslashes are converted, as the spec requires. Without it the new pattern would give `".."` the extension `"."`.

`parse` and the `posix`/`win32` versions needed no edits, because they call `extname`.
